name: code-review-comparison
description: Review and compare three implementations of the same feature

promptLevels.beginner: compare TypeScript, JavaScript, and JavaScript+JSDoc implementations of a shopping cart
promptLevels.intermediate: review three shopping cart implementations and identify differences in type safety and maintainability
promptLevels.advanced:
Compare the three implementations below in terms of type safety, maintainability, potential bugs, and developer experience:

Review the following three implementations of a shopping cart system

languageInstructions.typescript: Provide a detailed comparative analysis as markdown. Include a pros/cons table for each approach, specific code examples showing where TypeScript prevents bugs, and discuss scenarios where TypeScript's build overhead might not be justified.
languageInstructions.javascript: Provide analysis focusing on JavaScript's flexibility vs safety trade-offs. Include examples of runtime bugs that type systems would catch, discuss runtime validation strategies, and explain when pure JavaScript is the appropriate choice.
languageInstructions.javascript-jsdoc: Provide analysis highlighting JSDoc as a middle ground between TypeScript and plain JavaScript. Discuss IDE support quality, limitations compared to full TypeScript (no compile-time enforcement), and scenarios where JSDoc provides sufficient type safety without build tooling complexity.

variants.javascript: This task requires analyzing TypeScript code. Please review Implementation B from the TypeScript variant.
variants.javascript-jsdoc: This task requires analyzing TypeScript code. Please review Implementation C from the TypeScript variant.

performanceBenchmarks.name: parse-code-structure
performanceBenchmarks.code: const code = "class Test { constructor(name) { this.name = name; } getName() { return this.name; } }"; for (let i = 0; i < 1000; i++) { const hasClass = code.includes("class"); const hasConstructor = code.includes("constructor"); const hasMethods = code.match(/\w+\s*\(/g); }

performanceBenchmarks.name: analyze-complexity
performanceBenchmarks.code: const code = "function test() { for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) { if (i % 2 === 0) { console.log(i); } } }".repeat(100); const lines = code.split("\n"); const complexity = lines.filter(l => /\bif\b|\bfor\b|\bwhile\b/.test(l)).length;
